translation: Target defines (names, without proving or asserting) the following proposition: For every natural number m, assuming m ≠ 0 (the explicit NeZero m hypothesis) and 2 ≤ m, there does not exist a synchronous Boolean-input, Boolean-output system N (of type S1 Bool Bool) that simultaneously satisfies two conditions: (1) its dependency graph is acyclic (N.D9), and (2) it has the exact same input-output behavior on all finite Boolean sequences as the single-node modulo-m counter d26 m (S1.D6 N (d26 m)). In detail: a system N of type S1 Bool Bool consists of a finite type of nodes (A1, equipped with a Fintype instance), a state type A3 n for each node n (which is not required to be finite or bounded in size), an initial state a4 n in A3 n for each node, an update function a5 assigning to each node n, global state σ (an assignment of a state in A3 k to every node k), and Boolean input x a new state in A3 n, and a Boolean readout function a6 on global states. In condition (1), a directed dependency edge goes from node m to node n (N.D8 m n) if and only if there exist two arbitrary (not necessarily reachable) global states σ and σ' that agree on every node k ≠ m and a Boolean input x such that node n's updated states differ (N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x); acyclicity (N.D9) requires that for every node n there is no non-empty directed chain of one or more such edges from n back to n (so both multi-step cycles and self-dependencies are forbidden). In condition (2), N is run on a finite list xs of Booleans by starting from the initial global state a4, updating all nodes synchronously from left to right for each element of xs, and finally applying a6; S1.D6 N (d26 m) requires that for every finite list xs of Booleans (of arbitrary length, including the empty list), this Boolean output equals that of d26 m, which has a single node with state space Fin m initialized to 0, increments its state by 1 modulo m on input true and leaves it unchanged on input false, and outputs true if and only if its final state is 0 (equivalently, if and only if the number of true entries in xs is divisible by m).

divergences.description: The formal definition S1 requires the set of units A1 to be finite (Fintype A1), whereas the description speaks only of 'no network' without explicitly stating finiteness. Finiteness of A1 is mathematically essential for Target to hold (an infinite acyclic network could match d26 m on all finite input sequences), though 'network' is standardly understood to be finite in this context.

Target restricts to synchronous deterministic Boolean-input, Boolean-output systems (S1 Bool Bool) and formalizes 'the counter modulo m' (d26 m) as a machine that increments on true, holds on false, and outputs a Boolean indicating whether the count of true inputs is 0 mod m (rather than outputting the residue in Fin m directly). As a non-existence claim, fixing this 1-bit divisibility readout is a specific modeling choice that actually makes the impossibility result stronger than for a full-residue readout.

Dependence between units (S1.D7) is defined by quantifying over all global states, including unreachable ones, so S1.D9 excludes networks whose update functions have a cycle only on unreachable states rather than only on reachable dynamics.

The description refers to 'a layered feedforward network as in Doerig et al.', whereas the cited excerpt [P-D51a] only mentions 'feedforward systems' (contrasted with 'recurrent systems') without explicitly describing them as 'layered' or specifying whether units can depend on themselves; however, the description properly qualifies the no-self-dependence condition as 'the author's rendering'.

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the author's non-existence claim about acyclic networks matching a modulo-m counter over all finite input sequences, and the description accurately reports Hanson and Walker's self-dependent feed-forward circuit while only mildly extrapolating beyond the quoted Doerig et al. excerpt. The only discrepancies are minor modeling and presentational details, notably the implicit finiteness of the unit set in S1 and the specific Boolean readout model of the counter.
